title: Sunset Session

conditions.headline: Tech Wipeout as AI Worries Break the Wave
conditions.summary: Stocks opened higher, then slid all day as AI spending fears hit chipmakers and software. The Nasdaq fell 2.1% and posted its worst week since late June, while energy rallied with oil.

sections.title: Closing Bell
items: Dow slipped 0.34% to 52,002.41; Russell 2000 lost about 1.7% to roughly 2,720.
Stocks opened higher, then sold off on worries about how AI spending and debt get paid for.
Tech was the worst sector, down about 3%; energy led, up about 2.5% with oil.
Roughly two of every three stocks fell, and the S&P ended a 55-day run without a 1% drop.
For the week, the Nasdaq fell about 4.5% and the S&P about 2%, while the Dow gained.

sections.title: Macro & Fed
items: September import prices rose 1.1%, above the 0.8% expected; export prices jumped 2.2%.
Industrial output rose 0.7% versus 0.4% expected; capacity use hit 76.9%.
Brent settled at $109.86, its highest since May, on Strait of Hormuz attacks; WTI near $99.
10-year yield held near 5.10%, about 15 basis points lower for the week.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, in Bangkok, said he does not prejudge meetings.
Futures see low odds of an October hike but still price a likely hike by December.

sections.title: Biggest Movers
items: CRWV (CoreWeave): about -12% — worries over its roughly $50 billion debt load.
PLTR (Palantir): about -7% — reversed a record breakout.
AMD (Advanced Micro Devices): -6% — chip stocks fell for an eighth straight day.
MU (Micron): -5.6% — memory chips slid with the semiconductor selloff.
META (Meta Platforms): -3.7% — caught in the AI spending scare.
TWLO (Twilio): about -8% — profit-taking after joining the S&P 500.
XOM (Exxon Mobil): +2.5% — rode higher oil prices.
CVX (Chevron): +2.6% — energy led the market.

sections.title: Earnings Today & Tonight
items: Travelers: core EPS $9.18 vs $7.43 expected; dipped early on catastrophe losses, closed up about 1.5%.
Regions: adjusted EPS $0.73 vs $0.66 expected.
M&T Bank: adjusted EPS $5.08 beat, but net interest income missed.
Citizens Financial: EPS $1.41 and a 13% dividend increase.
Alcoa rose about 2.5% after topping forecasts; J.B. Hunt missed as costs outran revenue growth.
No major companies reported after today's close.

sections.title: Business News
items: Proofpoint agreed to buy Varonis for $49.75 a share in cash, about $6.3 billion.
Tesla unveiled a redesigned Roadster, slated for production in 2028.
Netflix named Peter Rice chief content officer amid layoffs.
MSCI proposed rules that could drop Strategy (MSTR) from its global indexes.
Reports say investors are resisting Anthropic's planned $2 trillion valuation ahead of a November IPO.

sections.title: On Deck
items: Markets are closed for the weekend; the next session is Monday, Oct. 19.
Monday 9:00 AM CT: NAHB Housing Market Index for October.
Before the open Monday: Fifth Third Bancorp, Cleveland-Cliffs.
After the close Monday: Steel Dynamics, W.R. Berkley, Crown Holdings, AGNC, Zions.
No Fed speakers are on Monday's calendar.

It's Friday, October sixteenth, twenty twenty-six, and this is your Sunset Session, the full wrap of today's market. The sun is sinking over the water and the last set of the week just rolled through. Gus the wonder dog has guarded the cabana deck all afternoon. Say good evening, Gus! Here's the final set, and it was a gnarly wipeout for tech. The S and P five hundred fell one point one percent to seven thousand six hundred fifty-nine. The Nasdaq dropped two point one percent to twenty-six thousand one hundred forty. The Dow slipped a third of a percent to fifty-two thousand two. The Russell two thousand lost one point seven percent. Stocks opened higher, then slid all day on worries about paying for the A I spending boom. Tech was the worst sector, down about three percent. Energy led, up about two and a half. For the week, the Nasdaq fell about four and a half percent, its worst since late June. Now the wind and weather. Oil was the big swell. Brent hit about one hundred ten dollars, its highest since May, on attacks near the Strait of Hormuz. U S crude rose two and a half percent to near ninety-nine. Chevron rode that swell to the beach, up two and a half percent. Gus, that's worth a biscuit! Here you go, buddy! The ten year yield held near five point one percent. The fear gauge jumped twenty-one percent to near twenty. Import prices rose one point one percent, above forecasts, and industrial output beat too. Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said he does not prejudge meetings. Traders still see a likely hike by December. In the lineup, CoreWeave fell twelve percent on debt worries. Palantir dropped seven. A M D slid six and Micron lost five and a half as chips fell for an eighth day. Twilio dropped about eight on profit taking. Exxon and Alcoa each gained two and a half. When the hype fades, the hodads wash out first. On the tide chart, Travelers crushed estimates and closed up one and a half percent. Regions and M and T Bank beat profit forecasts, and Citizens raised its dividend thirteen percent. J B Hunt missed as costs outran revenue. Beach talk. Proofpoint will buy Varonis for about six point three billion dollars in cash. Tesla showed off a new Roadster for twenty twenty-eight. And Netflix named a new chief content officer. Tomorrow's forecast. The market rests for the weekend, so the next session is Monday. At nine A M Central we get home builder sentiment. Fifth Third reports before the open, and Steel Dynamics and W R Berkley report after the close. Got a stock, an E T F or a futures contract on your mind?
